intended_object: Given a ring isomorphism e : R ≃ ∏ᵢ M_{κᵢ}(Dᵢ), this is the i-th "row" right R-module D_i^{κ_i}. R acts on it through e and projection to the i-th block, by right multiplication of row vectors by matrices. It is bundled as a finitely generated projective right R-module (a left Rᵐᵒᵖ-module). For division rings Dᵢ these are the simple right modules of the semisimple ring R. The description comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes `matrixBlockModule D κ i`. That module is the product over j of right modules over the matrix rings M_{κⱼ}(Dⱼ). Its i-th factor is the row module κᵢ → Dᵢ with the right matrix action (`toRightMatrixModCat` applied to Dᵢ as a right Dᵢ-module). Every other factor is the zero module `PUnit`.

The body lifts the carrier with `ULift` and restricts scalars along `e.op`. So r ∈ R acts by x ↦ x · (e r)ᵢ, which the `_smul_down` lemma confirms by `rfl`. The finite-projective proof field is a proof obligation, transported along the equivalence of module categories; it adds no data.

This is exactly the standard i-th row module of a ring presented as a product of matrix rings. It works over arbitrary coefficient rings Dᵢ, which is already general; division rings are needed only for simplicity. The ULift only fixes universes and does not change the module.

The construction depends on the given decomposition e, so it is a specific object, not a general notion that Mathlib has in broader form. I found no Mathlib counterpart for this row module.
